@Mario Carneiro I'm making some progress towards finishing iProp, but I'm a little stuck on one part and wondering what you think. Your definition of OFunctor is a typeclass on top of functions (Type _ -> Type _ -> Type _) rather than the bundled Iris version (COFE -> COFE -> OFE). I'm not sure how to write an OFunctor in the case that the result type is only defined when the input types are COFE's.

The particular difficulty here comes when defining uPred, which in Rocq is parameterized by a UCMRA. If I define a bundled version of uPred (like how it is in my branch right now), then the OFunctor is only defined when the input types are COFE's. On the other hand, when I define an unbundled version (ie. moving the uPred_mono field to a separate typeclass so I can remove the UCMRA requirement from uPred) the type is no longer complete, and I cannot prove that uPred is a COFE.

Have you (or anyone) seen an issue like this before? I couldn't figure this issue out when I was working in Eileen either. The code at the bottom of my branch illustrates the issue concretely.
hm, I was rather hoping that such functions would not come up
Yeah. FWIW the unbundled version seems to work fine with the other oFunctors I've tried (though I'm not finished with those yet either).
I pushed a fix, allowing the functor to depend on OFE structure
I can add COFE structure too if needed, but I prefer to keep it as loose as reasonably possible

Nice! Thanks for doing that, I'm a little surprised it was fixable!!

I believe that dependence on COFE is necessary. The reason why is because the uPred OFunctor looks like

def uPredOF F [URFunctor F] (A : Type _) (B : Type _) : Type _ :=
  @uPred (F B A) (@URFunctor.cmra F _ B A sorry sorry)

so we need F B A to be a UCMRA. We get that from the URFunctor field

class URFunctor (F : Type _ → Type _ → Type _) where
  cmra [COFE α] [COFE β] : UCMRA (F α β)
   -- ...

which requires the arguments to be COFEs.
why is that there though?
Are you asking why URFunctors require COFEs rather than OFE's?
yes
Every URFunctor is an OFunctor which has the same restriction. I do not know why OFunctors have this requirement off the top of my head.
indeed, one can just replace COFE by OFE everywhere in OFunctor and it still works
I suspect we just don't have enough examples to see the rationale
maybe we should just downgrade everything to OFE now and that way we'll notice when something gets stuck later
intuitively, COFE "shouldn't" matter since it's just a proposition and not data
I agree that we should try with just OFE. If you're confident that it's easy to change after the fact then yeah, we might as well do some destructive testing on Iris (lol)
yeah, upgrading/downgrading these typeclasses has very little impact on most proofs

Mario Carneiro said:

intuitively, COFE "shouldn't" matter since it's just a proposition and not data

oh wait, that's a lie. COFE's have a compl field which is data (although I suspect it won't be computable in most cases)
A relevant snippet from Iris From the Ground Up: Screenshot 2025-04-05 at 5.02.57 PM.png
sounds like it is the right idea to start with OFEs and upgrade as needed then

I'm evaluating whether I can migrate my hand-rolled guarded recursion framework (for my private work on https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.02778) to iris-lean and am currently stuck on the issue that nested Fix (fun x => ... Fix (fun y => ... x...) ...) needs IsCOFE for the type of x. Specifically, the domain equation is

    Trace V ≅ V ⊕ ▶Trace V
    D       ≅ ▶D -n> Trace (▶D)

The problem is that Trace V recurses directly into V, so it is only defined when V is already a COFE (at least the AI says so, and it convinced me). The outer Fix for D however doesn't give COFEness for ▶D to Trace; hence type error.

But as instFixFunctorContractiveOfOFunctor in the following MWE shows, I think we can (strictly) generalize the type of Fix to accomodate such nested equations. Note that this new notion of "FixFunctor" is an ad-hoc generalization of OFunctor and hence not COFunctor. Here it goes:

import Iris.Algebra.COFESolver

/-! # Standalone MWE (depends only on iris-lean)

Why the recursive-domain-equation solver `OFunctor.Fix` needs *complete* (COFE)
inputs, via a stateful domain with a trace that has `ret`; and that moving the
solver to COFE inputs loses no generality.

    Trace V ≅ V ⊕ ▶Trace V          -- `ret v` returns a value, or one ▶ step
    D       ≅ ▶D -n> Trace (▶D)      -- stateful: state ↦ trace -/

open Iris Iris.COFE OFE

namespace TraceMWE
universe u

/-! ## A trace with `ret`, built by iris-lean's existing (OFE-indexed) solver -/

abbrev TraceF (V : Type) [OFE V] : OFunctorPre.{0} :=
  SumOF (constOF V) (LaterOF IdOF)

instance (V : Type) [OFE V] : Inhabited (TraceF V (ULift Unit) (ULift Unit)) :=
  ⟨.inr (Later.next default)⟩

abbrev Trace (V : Type) [COFE V] : Type := OFunctor.Fix (TraceF V)

/-! ## 1+2. The need for COFE

`ret v` makes `v : V` a *direct summand*, so a Cauchy chain `ret v₀, ret v₁, …`
converges only if `V` does: `Trace`'s very type requires completeness. -/

#check (Trace : (V : Type) → [COFE V] → Type)        -- note the `[COFE V]`

example (V : Type) [COFE V] : Type := Trace V         -- ✓ defined for complete V
-- example (V : Type) [OFE V]  : Type := Trace V      -- ✗ "failed to synthesize COFE V"

/-- Hence the stateful domain `D ≅ ▶D -n> Trace (▶D)` has a signature definable
    only on COFEs. As an `OFunctorPre` it does not typecheck, so the OFE-indexed
    `OFunctor.Fix` cannot solve it:

      `abbrev DSigBad : OFunctorPre := fun α β _ _ => ▶α -n> Trace (▶β)`  -- ✗

    (`Trace (▶β)` needs `COFE (▶β)`, unavailable from the `[OFE β]` that
    `OFunctorPre` provides). It is, however, a COFE-indexed functor: -/
abbrev DSig : ∀ α β [COFE α] [COFE β], Type :=
  fun α β _ _ => Later α -n> Trace (Later β)

/-! ## 3. `FixFunctor` — what the solver takes — and no loss of generality

`FixFunctor` is the input to the (COFE-input) recursive-domain solver: a locally
non-expansive bifunctor `COFE^op × COFE → OFE` (OFE-valued like `OFunctor`, just
on COFE inputs; completeness of the solution comes from the diagonal `IsCOFE`
side-condition, as for `OFunctor.Fix`). It is *not* an endofunctor on COFEs — the
name says only "what `Fix` takes". -/

class FixFunctor (F : ∀ α β [COFE α] [COFE β], Type u) where
  cofe [COFE α] [COFE β] : OFE (F α β)
  map [COFE α₁] [COFE α₂] [COFE β₁] [COFE β₂] :
    (α₂ -n> α₁) → (β₁ -n> β₂) → F α₁ β₁ -n> F α₂ β₂
  map_ne [COFE α₁] [COFE α₂] [COFE β₁] [COFE β₂] :
    NonExpansive₂ (@map α₁ α₂ β₁ β₂ _ _ _ _)
  map_id [COFE α] [COFE β] (x : F α β) : map (@Hom.id α _) (@Hom.id β _) x ≡ x
  map_comp [COFE α₁] [COFE α₂] [COFE α₃] [COFE β₁] [COFE β₂] [COFE β₃]
    (f : α₂ -n> α₁) (g : α₃ -n> α₂) (f' : β₁ -n> β₂) (g' : β₂ -n> β₃) (x : F α₁ β₁) :
    map (f.comp g) (g'.comp f') x ≡ map g g' (map f f' x)

attribute [reducible, instance] FixFunctor.cofe

class FixFunctorContractive (F : ∀ α β [COFE α] [COFE β], Type u) extends FixFunctor F where
  map_contractive [COFE α₁] [COFE α₂] [COFE β₁] [COFE β₂] :
    Contractive (Function.uncurry (@FixFunctor.map F _ α₁ α₂ β₁ β₂ _ _ _ _))

/-- Restrict an `OFunctor` to COFE inputs (input completeness simply unused). -/
def asCOFE (F : ∀ α β [OFE α] [OFE β], Type u) : ∀ α β [COFE α] [COFE β], Type u :=
  fun α β _ _ => F α β

/-- **No loss of generality:** every contractive `OFunctor` is a contractive
    `FixFunctor`. So a COFE-input solver accepts strictly more functors (`DSig`)
    while still accepting every old one. -/
instance instFixFunctorContractiveOfOFunctor
    {F : ∀ α β [OFE α] [OFE β], Type u} [OFunctorContractive F] :
    FixFunctorContractive (asCOFE F) where
  cofe := OFunctor.cofe
  map := OFunctor.map
  map_ne := OFunctor.map_ne
  map_id := OFunctor.map_id
  map_comp := OFunctor.map_comp
  map_contractive := OFunctorContractive.map_contractive

example {F : ∀ α β [OFE α] [OFE β], Type} [OFunctorContractive F] :
    FixFunctorContractive (asCOFE F) := inferInstance

end TraceMWE
Meanwhile I'll just work with my own copy of COFESolver, the proof of which work essentially unchanged with the generalized notion

Sebastian Graf said:

The problem is that Trace V recurses directly into V, so it is only defined when V is already a COFE (at least the AI says so, and it convinced me). The outer Fix for D however doesn't give COFEness for ▶D to Trace; hence type error.

That is a good example!
Hm, I think the correct way would be to have OFunctor and OFunctorPre to be defined on COFEs only.
In principle, it should be fine to keep RFunctor and other CMRA-related functors to work on OFEs, since UPred is always complete (for example, that the reason why Transfinite Iris works with solver of type OFE^op \times OFE \to COFE). I will think today on how to fix it. Thanks for the report!

Markus de Medeiros said:

Ah, nice. Sergei Stepanenko how does this relate to your work?

In my small prototype, I didn't even have a definition of OFE, only COFE :^)

Hi again,
I've created a PR for this problem. The idea is to change OFunctorPre to accept COFE parameters only (which also matches the original Rocq version better).
Informally, that should not break any clients, because if a client functor was defined on OFEs, it should just pull OFE part of COFE now.

It solves part of the problems that @Sebastian Graf encountered, when using it (the current one carries an implicit requirement to be defined on OFEs).
There was another issue with this particular example: strictly speaking functor for D is not something that is covered by existing class of functors, since it requires functoriality of Trace, which is itself defined as a solution to another equation. In this particular case, it is possible to show that it is functorial, because Trace is uses only covariant argument, but in more general cases it can be a blocker (in both versions of Iris).
I've showed its functoriality by guarded recursion (please see attached), but it probably be nice to figure out if it's possible to generalize it a bit. I've tried to see if it possible to use uniqueness of solution, but it doesn't give much in this case, so probably there is no reason to add the uniqueness to the PR.

@Sebastian Graf could you please take a look if the things below works for your use case? I think if Trace doesn't use contravariant things, then it should work, but otherwise it might require something else.

Code

import Iris.Algebra.COFESolver

open Iris Iris.COFE OFE

namespace TraceMWE

abbrev TraceF (V : Type _) [OFE V] : OFunctorPre :=
  SumOF (constOF V) (LaterOF IdOF)

instance (V : Type _) [OFE V] : Inhabited (TraceF V (ULift Unit) (ULift Unit)) :=
  ⟨.inr (Later.next default)⟩

abbrev Trace (V : Type _) [COFE V] : Type _ := OFunctor.Fix (TraceF V)

example (V : Type _) [COFE V] : Type _ := Trace V

section Functoriality
open OFunctor

@[simp] theorem laterMap_apply {A B : Type _} [OFE A] [OFE B] (t : A -n> B) (x : Later A) :
    laterMap t x = Later.next (t x.car) := rfl

theorem laterMap_id {A : Type _} [OFE A] : laterMap (Hom.id : A -n> A) = Hom.id := rfl

theorem laterMap_comp {A B C : Type _} [OFE A] [OFE B] [OFE C] (g : B -n> C) (f : A -n> B) :
    laterMap (g.comp f) = (laterMap g).comp (laterMap f) := rfl

theorem laterMap_ne {A B : Type _} [OFE A] [OFE B] {n} {t t' : A -n> B} (h : t ≡{n}≡ t') :
    laterMap t ≡{n}≡ laterMap t' := fun x _ hm => (h x.car).lt hm

theorem laterMap_contractive {A B : Type _} [OFE A] [OFE B] {n} {t t' : A -n> B}
    (h : DistLater n t t') : laterMap t ≡{n}≡ laterMap t' := fun x m hm => h m hm x.car

variable {V₁ V₂ V₃ : Type _} [COFE V₁] [COFE V₂] [COFE V₃]

def traceMapBody (h : V₁ -n> V₂) (t : Trace V₁ -n> Trace V₂) : Trace V₁ -n> Trace V₂ :=
  Fix.fold.comp (Hom.comp ⟨Sum.map h (laterMap t), inferInstance⟩ Fix.unfold)

theorem traceMapBody_contractive (h : V₁ -n> V₂) : Contractive (traceMapBody h) where
  distLater_dist {n t t'} H := by
    have hlt : laterMap t ≡{n}≡ laterMap t' := laterMap_contractive H
    intro x
    refine Fix.fold.ne.1 ?_
    show Sum.map h (laterMap t) (Fix.unfold x) ≡{n}≡ Sum.map h (laterMap t') (Fix.unfold x)
    rcases Fix.unfold x with a | b
    · exact .rfl
    · exact hlt b

def traceMap (h : V₁ -n> V₂) : Trace V₁ -n> Trace V₂ :=
  haveI : Contractive (traceMapBody h) := traceMapBody_contractive h
  ContractiveHom.fixpoint (Function.toContractiveHom (traceMapBody h))

theorem traceMap_unfold (h : V₁ -n> V₂) : traceMap h ≡ traceMapBody h (traceMap h) := by
  haveI : Contractive (traceMapBody h) := traceMapBody_contractive h
  exact fixpoint_unfold (Function.toContractiveHom (traceMapBody h))

theorem traceMap_id : traceMap (Hom.id : V₁ -n> V₁) ≡ Hom.id := by
  haveI : Contractive (traceMapBody (Hom.id : V₁ -n> V₁)) := traceMapBody_contractive _
  refine (fixpoint_unique (f := Function.toContractiveHom (traceMapBody Hom.id)) ?_).symm
  intro x
  refine (Fix.fold_unfold x).symm.trans (NonExpansive.eqv ?_)
  show Fix.unfold x ≡ Sum.map Hom.id (laterMap Hom.id) (Fix.unfold x)
  rcases Fix.unfold x with a | b <;> exact .rfl

theorem traceMap_comp (g : V₂ -n> V₃) (f : V₁ -n> V₂) :
    traceMap (g.comp f) ≡ (traceMap g).comp (traceMap f) := by
  haveI : Contractive (traceMapBody (g.comp f)) := traceMapBody_contractive _
  refine (fixpoint_unique (f := Function.toContractiveHom (traceMapBody (g.comp f))) ?_).symm
  intro x
  have e₂ : Fix.unfold (traceMap f x) ≡ Sum.map f (laterMap (traceMap f)) (Fix.unfold x) :=
    (NonExpansive.eqv (traceMap_unfold f x)).trans (Fix.unfold_fold _)
  refine (traceMap_unfold g (traceMap f x)).trans (NonExpansive.eqv (f := Fix.fold) ?_)
  refine (NonExpansive.eqv (f := Sum.map g (laterMap (traceMap g))) e₂).trans ?_
  show Sum.map g (laterMap (traceMap g)) (Sum.map f (laterMap (traceMap f)) (Fix.unfold x))
      ≡ Sum.map (g.comp f) (laterMap ((traceMap g).comp (traceMap f))) (Fix.unfold x)
  rcases Fix.unfold x with a | b <;> exact .rfl

theorem traceMap_ne {n} {h h' : V₁ -n> V₂} (e : h ≡{n}≡ h') : traceMap h ≡{n}≡ traceMap h' := by
  haveI : Contractive (traceMapBody h) := traceMapBody_contractive h
  haveI : Contractive (traceMapBody h') := traceMapBody_contractive h'
  refine NonExpansive.ne (f := ContractiveHom.fixpoint) ?_
  intro T x
  refine Fix.fold.ne.1 ?_
  show Sum.map h (laterMap T) (Fix.unfold x) ≡{n}≡ Sum.map h' (laterMap T) (Fix.unfold x)
  rcases Fix.unfold x with a | b
  · exact e a
  · exact .rfl

end Functoriality

open OFunctor in
abbrev TraceLaterOF : OFunctorPre := fun _ β _ _ => Trace (Later β)

open OFunctor in
instance : OFunctor TraceLaterOF where
  ofe := inferInstance
  map _ g := traceMap (laterMap g)
  map_ne := ⟨fun _ _ _ _ _ _ hg => traceMap_ne (laterMap_ne hg)⟩
  map_id x := traceMap_id x
  map_comp _ _ f' g' x := traceMap_comp (laterMap g') (laterMap f') x

open OFunctor OFunctorContractive in
instance : OFunctorContractive TraceLaterOF where
  map_contractive.1 {_} _ _ h :=
    traceMap_ne (laterMap_contractive fun m hm => (h m hm).2)

open OFunctor in
abbrev DSig : OFunctorPre := HomOF (LaterOF IdOF) TraceLaterOF

instance : OFunctorContractive DSig := inferInstance

abbrev D : Type _ := OFunctor.Fix DSig

open OFunctor in
def D.iso : OFE.Iso D (Later D -n> Trace (Later D)) := by
  refine ⟨Fix.unfold (F := DSig), Fix.fold (F := DSig), ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro x; exact Fix.unfold_fold (F := DSig) x
  · intro x; exact Fix.fold_unfold (F := DSig) x

end TraceMWE

So the domain equation I want to solve is

D  ≅  Heap (▶D) -n> Trace (Value (▶D) × Heap (▶D))

with the pieces

Heap X   = GenMap X                                  -- finite ℕ-keyed maps (the store)
Trace V  ≅ V  ⊕  (Event × ▶Trace V)  ⊕  ▶Trace V      -- ret | step | invis
Value X  ≅ stuck  ⊕  (X -n> X)  ⊕  (ConTag × List X)  -- stuck | fn | con

and with the changes to OFunctor, it should work just fine!
